title: Deformation Professionnelle
hook: A favorite tool can make every problem arrive in the shape of its handle.
counterintuition: Expertise can narrow sight as well as sharpen it; name the professional lens, then force a second model into the choice.
tryThisNow: Name the tool your role reaches for first. Before using it, ask which other discipline would frame the same problem differently.
keyTakeaway: A professional lens can turn a real problem into the kind your specialty prefers. Add a second model before the tool chooses.

breakdown.fastRead: The lab notebook at the hotel desk belongs to Ana, who sees every guest problem as a price curve. Families need rooms, not only a better curve. The desk lead can point to the families still waiting. Legal can name the refund risk. She writes role lens on the notebook, adds desk and legal checks to the rule, and changes the night's choice before the manager calls guests.
breakdown.deepRead:
A specialty trains your eye. That is useful. It helps you see patterns other people miss. It also tempts you to see every problem as a version of the work you already know how to do.

Deformation professionnelle is the bend a profession puts into judgment. The lawyer sees liability. The engineer sees process. The marketer sees message. The doctor sees diagnosis. The finance lead sees incentives. Each lens can be right about something and wrong about the whole.

A tool is not a world.

The correction is to add a second model before the team acts. Ask how another discipline would frame the issue. What would operations, psychology, safety, law, design, or economics notice? Which facts become larger when your usual tool is not allowed to answer first?

This matters because expertise often has status in the room. Once the specialist names the problem, everyone else may start solving that version. A hotel overbooking issue becomes a pricing issue. A pediatric appointment default becomes a scheduling issue. A ferry fog rule becomes a water-sample issue. The first lens may be useful, but it should not get a monopoly.
breakdown.fullRead:
The contract redline in the chemicals plant incentive review is covered with neat comments from legal. Carla, the plant manager, can see why. The bonus clause might expose the company if operators cut a safety step. But if the meeting stays inside the legal frame, it will miss the production model that rewards speed and the safety model that tracks near misses. The contract matters. It is not the whole plant.

A profession gives you a map, and a map leaves things out. The danger is not having a map. The danger is forgetting that it is one map among several. Deformation professionnelle starts when the trained lens becomes the only lens allowed to define the problem.

What would this look like if your favorite tool were locked away?

Munger argued for models across a wide range of disciplines because no single specialty can carry the weight of the world. A person with only one model keeps translating reality into the language of that model. Sometimes that translation is elegant. Sometimes it is expensive.

A farm rainfall projection shows the trap. Lorraine, trained in finance, sees crop insurance as a hedge question. The agronomist sees soil moisture. The neighbor sees labor timing. The case file needs all three. If Lorraine marks the Munger risk and brings those models into the same choice, the farm gets a plan. If she lets finance answer alone, the hedge may look tidy while the field still fails.

The second model is not decoration.

A car-rental insurance upsell gives the retail version. Melissa reads the sensor graph from the rental fleet and sees a technical risk score. The counter staff see hurried travelers declining coverage because the explanation sounds like a trap. The specialty view says improve the risk model. The service view says change the script. Both may be needed. A single lens would choose too soon.

The practical correction is a lens check. First, name your default specialty. Second, state how it frames the problem. Third, invite one model that would disagree or enlarge the frame. Fourth, decide only after the competing model has changed at least one fact, risk, or action on the page.

The limit is that not every problem needs a committee. A surgeon should not ask a marketer how to make an incision. A ferry captain should not run a philosophy seminar in fog. But even urgent work can ask a compact second question: what is my specialty making easy to see, and what is it hiding?

Before the choice moves forward, make the lens visible. Put the model name on the page. Put one rival model beside it. If the same action survives both, move. If the action changes, the problem was never just the shape your tool first gave it.

examples.title: Ana adds the front-desk lens
examples.scenario: A lab notebook sits beside the hotel overbooking screen in Lisbon at 8:05 p.m. Ana, the pricing analyst, must decide whether to solve the night's room shortage with a yield model alone. She marks professional lens on the notebook, asks the front-desk lead and legal clerk for their constraints, and changes the overbooking rule before guest calls begin.
examples.whatToDo: Balance revenue math with service and legal constraints before altering capacity.

implementationPlan.coreSkill: Name the professional lens, add a rival model, and decide only after the second model changes the page.

ifThenPlans.plan: If one expert frame dominates, then I will ask which model is missing before approving it.
If a tool optimizes one metric, then I will check who experiences the side effect.
If a model explains risk, then I will test whether the person receiving the offer understands it.
If time is short, then I will ask one compact second-lens question instead of opening a broad debate.

implementationPlan.twentyFourHourChallenge: Take one recommendation from your own specialty. Write the lens it uses and one rival lens that would change a fact or action.
implementationPlan.weeklyPractice: Once a week, review a decision where your role supplied the first answer and ask what model never got invited.
